collections/set#

Immutable sets with deterministic traversal order.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let empty is List<string> = EmptyList();
let input = empty
    .prefix("third")
    .prefix("first")
    .prefix("second")
    .prefix("first");
let names = OrderedSet(values: input);
// traversal: "first", "second", "third"

Description#

Immutable sets with deterministic traversal order.

OrderedSet keeps the first occurrence of every value:

addition() and difference() are nouns: each denotes another immutable set. Existing sets remain unchanged and may share their origins:

let extended = names.addition("fourth");
let shortened = extended.difference("second");

Binary set objects preserve deterministic order:

let either = Union(left: preferred, right: fallback);
let common = Intersection(left: preferred, right: fallback);
let only_preferred = Difference(left: preferred, right: fallback);
let changed = SymmetricDifference(left: preferred, right: fallback);

Union traverses the left set first and then unseen right values. Intersection and Difference retain left order. SymmetricDifference emits left-only values followed by right-only values.

OrderedSet takes any T with runtime equality, arrays included, so it uses strict runtime equality and linear membership instead of pretending to be a HashSet. When the values are map keys — scalars, enums or value objects (#212) — KeyedSet keeps them in a map, in key order, with logarithmic membership; the compiler checks that its T is a key type (#242). Native opaque handles have no equality.

Set is conceptually the conjunction of Iterating<T> and Sizing. Until role composition exists, concrete sets explicitly implement all three roles.

object KeyedSet#

object KeyedSet<T> does Set<T>, Iterating<T>, Sizing

A set of map keys in key order (#242): membership is O(log n), and building one from n values is O(n log n).

let seen = KeyedSet(values: ["b", "a", "b"]);   // traversal: "a", "b"
seen.membership("a");                             // true
